title: Orbital Strike found its fire director
thesis: Turn a compact browser FPS into an authored aerospace operation with one unforgettable player-controlled moment.
summary: Orbital Strike moved from a sparse corridor prototype to a legible, atmospheric station assault built around charging and calling down an orbital penetrator.

comparisons.title: From title screen to mission briefing
comparisons.caption: The opening now establishes the orbital geometry, mission state, and visual language before the player enters the station.

before.alt: The original Orbital Strike start screen with a simple centered title and mission button.

after.alt: The revised fire-director mission briefing with a large orbital trajectory, telemetry, and launch control.

comparisons.title: From empty hallway to station machinery
comparisons.caption: A procedural octagonal interior, directional lighting, weapon model, and instrument-like HUD make the station readable as a place and a machine.

before.alt: The original gameplay view in a sparse rectangular station corridor.

after.alt: The revised gameplay view inside a teal-lit octagonal station corridor with weapon and tactical displays.

comparisons.title: A signature action the player owns
comparisons.caption: Exploration and combat now charge a targeted strike; the lock, beam, shockwave, and area damage make its arrival the run’s visual and mechanical payoff.

before.alt: The original Orbital Strike combat view without an orbital strike ability.

after.alt: A brilliant orbital penetrator beam and expanding shockwave hitting the station floor.

changes.title: The station became a machine
changes.body: Union-boundary corridors, repeating ribs, panels, floor lanes, and purposeful light sources replaced the generic room geometry with a coherent industrial language.

changes.title: The fantasy gained a verb
changes.body: Players earn strike charge through the mission, choose the impact point, and receive a readable lock-to-impact sequence with real area damage.

changes.title: The cockpit explains itself
changes.body: Heading, mission progress, strike state, prompts, pause and completion states, and touch controls now behave as one responsive flight-instrument system.

builderNote.quote: This is so much better than the old one
builderNote.context: Reaction after comparing the preserved pre-overhaul build with the fire-director second pass.

proof.label: Gameplay checks
proof.value: Collision, shooting, strike, pause, restart, touch, and mission completion

proof.label: Workstream boundary
proof.value: The Island remained separate and untouched

share.summary: See how Orbital Strike became a focused station assault with a player-targeted orbital penetrator as its defining moment.
